content: Tooth brushing refers to the process of cleaning teeth using a toothbrush. Proper tooth brushing, as supported by modern medical research, is essential for preventing dental caries (cavities), gingivitis, and periodontal disease, which is a major cause of tooth loss in adults, accounting for at least one-third of cases. Inadequate or infrequent brushing can lead to the calcification of minerals in saliva, resulting in the formation of tartar. Historically, tooth brushing has been a critical component of oral hygiene. For instance, ancient Egyptians used rudimentary toothbrushes made from twigs and leaves to clean their teeth. Similarly, other cultures, such as the Greeks, Romans, and Indians, employed twigs for dental cleaning, often fraying one end to enhance its ability to clean between teeth. The process of brushing teeth is vital for maintaining the cleanliness of both teeth and gums. It is recommended to use a toothbrush with soft, nylon, rounded bristles to avoid scratching or irritating the teeth and gums. The proper technique involves placing the toothbrush at a 45-degree angle against the gums and moving it gently up and down in short, tooth-wide strokes. All surfaces of the teeth should be brushed, including the outer, inner, and chewing surfaces. The toe of the toothbrush can be used to clean the inner surfaces of the front teeth with gentle up-and-down strokes. Additionally, brushing the tongue is important to remove bacteria and improve breath freshness. A toothbrush is a tool designed for cleaning teeth, consisting of a small brush attached to a handle. Toothpaste, often containing fluoride, is typically applied to the toothbrush to enhance its cleaning effectiveness. Toothbrushes are available in various bristle textures, sizes, and shapes. Most dental professionals recommend using a toothbrush labeled Soft, as firmer bristles can damage tooth enamel and irritate the gums, as noted by the American Dental Association. While most toothbrushes are made from synthetic fibers, natural toothbrushes are also used in some parts of the world. Toothpaste is a paste or gel dentifrice used to clean teeth and improve their appearance and health. It is almost always used in conjunction with a toothbrush. The use of toothpaste promotes good oral hygiene by aiding in the removal of dental plaque and food debris from teeth, helping to eliminate or mask bad breath (halitosis), and delivering active ingredients such as fluoride to prevent dental and gum diseases.
